_about: New verified records, 2026-11-24. Universities: on the NUC list of approved universities (existence and type); full profiles for three from Wikipedia. Schools: confirmed by their Wikipedia articles. Wording is our own.

u00.name: University of Nigeria, Nsukka
u00.h: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) is a federal university and the first indigenous, autonomous university in Nigeria. A law to set it up in the old Eastern Region was passed on 18 May 1955, championed by Nnamdi Azikiwe, who later became Nigeria's first president. Planners from the University of Exeter and Michigan State University surveyed the Nsukka site in 1958, and a provisional council chaired by Azikiwe was appointed in April 1959. The university formally opened on 7 October 1960, days after independence, as one of Nigeria's first-generation universities. It was modelled on the American system and was the first land-grant university in Africa, built around service to the country's practical needs.
u00.a: UNN is a public research university with 17 faculties and 102 academic departments, offering more than 108 undergraduate and 211 postgraduate programmes, including medicine, law, engineering, agriculture and the arts and sciences. It is regularly counted among the most respected universities in Nigeria.
u00.c: The main campus is in Nsukka, Enugu State. The university also has campuses in Enugu city and at Ituku-Ozalla in Enugu State, the site of its teaching hospital, and in Aba, Abia State.

u01.name: Lagos State University
u01.h: Lagos State University (LASU) is a public university owned by the Lagos State Government. It was established in 1983 during the administration of Governor Lateef Jakande, 'for the advancement of learning and establishment of academic excellence'. It was first conceived as a multi-campus, non-residential university, and it began with three faculties: Commerce and Business Administration, Law, and Medicine.
u01.a: LASU now serves more than 35,000 students and offers diploma, degree and postgraduate programmes, including an MBA. Faculties added over time include Arts, Education, Engineering, Social Sciences, Management Sciences, Science, and Communication and Media Studies, together with a School of Transport and a College of Medicine. It has hosted a World Bank Africa Centre of Excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Times Higher Education placed it among the world's top 600 universities in its 2020 rankings, and in 2021 named it the best young university in Nigeria.
u01.c: The main campus is at Ojo, on the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The College of Medicine is at Ikeja, and the Epe campus, on the north side of the Lekki Lagoon, houses engineering, agriculture, environmental sciences and pre-degree studies.

u02.name: University of Medical Sciences, Ondo
u02.h: The University of Medical Sciences, Ondo (UNIMED) is a specialised public university owned by the Ondo State Government. It was created by a law signed in 2014 by Governor Olusegun Mimiko and approved by the National Universities Commission in 2015. It is described as the third specialised medical university in Africa, and it was the first specialised medical university in Nigeria to be accredited by the National Universities Commission. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Professor Friday Okonofua, a gynaecologist and the founder of the Women's Health and Action Research Centre.
u02.a: UNIMED concentrates on medicine and the health sciences. It also runs an Institute of Community Health Innovation and Development.
u02.c: The university is in Ondo City, Ondo State, in south-western Nigeria.

s000.name: American International School of Lagos
s000.h: The American International School of Lagos (AISL) is an international school that follows an American curriculum, founded in 1964. It moved to its present campus on Victoria Island in 1981, on about 2.4 hectares (6 acres) of land leased from the government.
s000.a: AISL teaches students from preschool to grade 12, following the American system of education.
s000.c: The campus is on Victoria Island, Lagos.
s000.s: The school has more than 600 students. About 30 per cent are American, and the rest come from over 50 countries, with large groups from India, the United Kingdom, Nigeria, Canada, South Africa, Israel, Lebanon and the Netherlands.
s000.source_name: Wikipedia: American International School of Lagos

s001.name: Apata Memorial High School
s001.h: Apata Memorial High School is a privately owned school in Lagos run on military lines. It was founded in 1980 by S. O. Apata, a retired brigadier-general of the Nigerian Army.
s001.a: The school has about 1,550 pupils and 150 teachers, which gives it relatively small classes for a Lagos school of its size.
s001.s: It takes both boarding and day students, and its military-style discipline is part of daily life for boys and girls alike.

s002.name: Essence International School
s002.h: Essence International School (EIS) is an international school in Kaduna, founded in 1982.
s002.a: The school covers every stage of schooling: pre-nursery, nursery, primary and secondary education.
s002.c: It is on Kashim Ibrahim Road, near Sultan Road, in the Ungwan Rimi area of Kaduna.

s003.name: Air Force Military School, Jos
s003.h: Air Force Military School, Jos (AFMS) is a secondary school run by the Nigerian Air Force, established on 18 September 1980. By August 2022 it had graduated more than 3,794 'junior airmen', and many of its graduates have gone on to be commissioned officers in the army, air force and navy.
s003.a: AFMS combines a normal secondary curriculum, including subjects such as mathematics, physics, geography and French, with military training. Boys aged roughly 11 to 17 learn drill, map reading and interpretation, fieldcraft, compass and route marches, obstacle crossing, abseiling and weapons handling, as well as taking part in range practice, mock exercises and bush camps.
s003.c: The school is in Jos, Plateau State.
s003.s: Students are known as junior airmen, and the daily routine follows military discipline.
s003.source_name: Wikipedia: Air Force Military School, Jos

s004.name: Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta
s004.h: The Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta is an all-boys boarding school opened by the Nigerian Navy in 1990. By then, the Navy's only other secondary school, at Ojo in Lagos, could no longer take all the children of naval personnel who wanted places. The governor of Ogun State, Captain Mohammed Lawal, suggested the site of the defunct St Leo's Teachers' Training College at Ibara, Abeokuta, and the Navy appointed the school's first staff on 20 November 1990.
s004.a: The school offers academic secondary education together with military-style training. Admiral Murtala Nyako directed that, although it is a civilian school, it should be run as the equivalent of a military school.
s004.c: The campus is on the hilly Onikolobo site at Ibara, Abeokuta, Ogun State.
s004.source_name: Wikipedia: Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta

s005.name: Indian Language School
s005.h: The Indian Language School is a school in Lagos founded in 1982 to serve the city's growing Indian community. It comes under the High Commission of India in Nigeria and is managed by a board of trustees of business people. It began in converted houses at 11 Johnson Street, Ilupeju, and has since expanded by acquiring neighbouring properties. It is the only Indian school in Lagos.
s005.a: The school teaches from lower kindergarten to the 12th standard, and has entered students for the Indian CBSE board examinations for grades 10 and 12 since the late 1980s.
s005.c: The school is at Johnson Street, Ilupeju, Lagos, with a playground and football, basketball and volleyball courts.

s006.name: Loyola College, Ibadan
s006.h: Loyola College, Ibadan (LCI) is a boys' secondary school founded by Catholic missionaries in 1954 and now owned by the Oyo State Government. It has produced alumni in medicine, engineering, law, politics and the media.
s006.a: Students sit the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) at the end of senior secondary school. Old students support the school: in October 2023, for example, an alumnus paid the WAEC fees of six final-year students and sponsored UTME candidates.
s006.c: The college is on Old Ife Road in the Agodi area of Ibadan, Oyo State.

s007.name: St Anne's School, Ibadan
s007.h: St Anne's School, Ibadan is a girls' secondary school that can claim to be the oldest girls' secondary school in Nigeria. It traces its history to the CMS Female Institution, founded in Lagos on 1 May 1869 at the urging of Abigail Macaulay, daughter of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, so that Lagos families need not send their daughters abroad to study. That school, later the CMS Girls School, merged in 1950 with Kudeti Girls School in Ibadan, founded in 1899. The combined school was renamed St Anne's in honour of the missionary Anna Hinderer.
s007.a: The school started with sixteen pupils on what is now Broad Street, Lagos, under its first principal, Mrs Roper, and today provides secondary education for girls.
s007.c: The school is in Ibadan, Oyo State.

s008.name: Ijebu Ode Grammar School
s008.h: Ijebu Ode Grammar School (JOGS) is a boys' secondary school founded on 20 January 1913, which makes it one of the oldest secondary schools in Nigeria. The educationist Israel Oludotun Ransome-Kuti is among the figures associated with its history.
s008.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education for boys.
s008.c: It is in Ijebu-Ode local government area of Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.
s008.s: Students belong to six houses: Gansallo (blue), Johnson (red), Kuti (grey), Odumosu (green), Phillips (yellow) and School (purple).

s009.name: Olivet Baptist High School
s009.h: Olivet Baptist High School, formerly Oyo Baptist Boys' High School, is a Baptist secondary school affiliated with the Nigerian Baptist Convention. American Baptist missionaries founded it on 29 January 1945 in the old Baptist mission house at Oke-Isokun, Oyo, where the first Baptist missionary to Oyo had set up a mission post; that site is now the Baptist College of Theology. The school was widely known in the 1960s for excellence in both academics and sport.
s009.a: Olivet once prepared students for both O-level and A-level (Higher School Certificate) examinations; the A-level programme ended in 1989. It was one of the few schools outside Lagos with laboratories for the sciences, home economics, fine arts and music, and workshops for metalwork, woodwork and technical drawing.
s009.c: The school stands on a hilltop known as Olivet Heights in Oyo town, Oyo State, with hostels and staff quarters on campus.

s010.name: Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran
s010.h: Lagos State Model Junior College, Meiran is a state-owned junior secondary school. It was formed on 6 January 2003, when the Lagos State Ministry of Education split every secondary school in the state into separate junior (JSS1–3) and senior (SS1–3) schools. It came from Lagos State Model College, Meiran, founded on 19 February 1988; the same reform created junior model colleges at Badore, Igbonla, Kankon and Igbokuta. Its first principal, Mrs T. D. Kuti, led it until 2009.
s010.a: As a junior college it teaches the first three years of secondary school (JSS1 to JSS3), after which students move to senior secondary school.
s010.c: The school is at Oke-Odo, Meiran, in the north of Lagos.
s010.source_name: Wikipedia: Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran

s011.name: American International School of Abuja
s011.h: The American International School of Abuja (AISA) is a co-educational international day school founded in 1993 by a group of parents and US Embassy officials. They wanted a school that would prepare international and Nigerian students to continue their education under an American curriculum. In August 2006 it moved into a new purpose-built campus with room to grow.
s011.a: AISA teaches from preschool to grade 12, following a US-based curriculum, over a school year that runs from August to June with 180 teaching days. As enrolment grew from about 150 students in 2005 to about 470, it added a full high school programme.
s011.c: The school is in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.
s011.s: Its students come from more than 40 countries.
s011.source_name: Wikipedia: American International School of Abuja

s012.name: Binta International School
s012.h: Binta International School is part of a group of schools founded by Mrs Ehi Adenuga in Lagos. It opened in Ejigbo in 1994 and later moved to Ajao Estate, Isolo. Its name stands for 'Best In Nurturing Talents and Academics', its motto is 'excellence and discipline', and it gave its name to the school in the national television series Binta and Friends.
s012.a: The group runs a crèche, nursery, basic school and high school, and awards scholarships to deserving students each year. Its students have won competitions including the AIT Whizkid competition (1995), the 12th Unilever essay competition and the AIT debate competition (both 2000), and placed second in the Cowbell Lagos secondary school mathematics competition.
s012.c: The school is in Ajao Estate, Isolo, Lagos.

s013.name: A.D.R.A.O. International School
s013.h: Chief Abimbola Omololu-Mulele opened A.D.R.A.O. International School in 1963, which makes it one of Nigeria's longest-established independent schools. It takes both boys and girls.
s013.a: The school offers an independent, internationally oriented education.
s013.c: The school is on Victoria Island, Lagos.

s014.name: Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro
s014.h: Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro was founded in February 1963 by the government of the old Western Region, as an experiment in linking secondary education to the country's manpower needs after independence. It was set up with American support: Harvard University staff came through USAID, and the Ford Foundation funded the school until 1973. Similar comprehensive schools were proposed for Nigeria and Kenya at the same time.
s014.a: The school was designed to combine academic and practical education, giving priority to sixth-form science and adding technical streams at school-certificate level, unlike the purely academic grammar schools of the time.
s014.c: It is in Ayetoro, in the Egbado (Yewa) area of Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.

s015.name: Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos
s015.h: The French community in Lagos, through the Association Française du Nigeria, opened a French school in 1958. It moved between sites in Ikoyi and Victoria Island until 1987, when it settled in a purpose-built campus paid for partly by the French foreign ministry. In 1997 it became the Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos (LFLP).
s015.a: Pupils follow the French national curriculum from primary school to the end of secondary school. The lycée is part of the AEFE, the agency that runs France's worldwide network of schools abroad.
s015.c: The school is on Victoria Island, Lagos.
s015.source_name: Wikipedia: Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos

s016.name: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan
s016.h: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan was founded as Wesley College on 5 November 1905. It was originally a teacher-training institution, and one of its best-known students was Chief Obafemi Awolowo, the first premier of the Western Region. It is often described as one of the oldest secondary schools in Nigeria.
s016.a: Today it is a government-controlled, co-educational senior secondary school that prepares science students for the Senior School Certificate Examination.
s016.c: The college is in Ibadan, Oyo State.
s016.source_name: Wikipedia: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan

s017.name: School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada
s017.h: The School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada, formerly Government Gifted Secondary School, is a public secondary school established in 1993 to meet the educational needs of gifted students in the Federal Capital Territory. It began operating in 1994, and its motto is 'Knowledge for Excellence'.
s017.a: The school offers science, humanities and business streams at senior secondary level.
s017.c: It is in Gwagwalada, in the Federal Capital Territory.
s017.source_name: Wikipedia: School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada

s018.name: Mount Saint Gabriel's Secondary School
s018.h: Bishop James Hagan of the Catholic Diocese of Makurdi opened Mount Saint Gabriel's on 14 January 1964, giving Makurdi its first secondary school. It began as a day school for 63 boys from Tiv, Idoma, Igbo, Hausa and other communities, taught in temporary classrooms at Holy Ghost Parish, and moved to its permanent site in 1966. The civil war held back its growth, but it recovered and expanded in the 1970s. Today it is a Catholic boarding school for boys.
s018.a: MSG follows the national curriculum and prepares students for WAEC and NECO examinations, and it is known for academic excellence in Benue State.
s018.c: The school is in Makurdi, the capital of Benue State, near Government College.
s018.source_name: Wikipedia: Mount Saint Gabriel's Secondary School

s019.name: Grundtvig International Secondary School
s019.h: Dr Kachi E. Ozumba (1942–2011) founded Grundtvig International Secondary School in 1998. He named it after N. F. S. Grundtvig, the Danish thinker behind the folk high school movement, and based the school on Grundtvig's idea of education for life.
s019.a: Grundtvig takes boys and girls aged 12 to 18. Its WAEC results have repeatedly placed it among the ten best schools in Nigeria, and it ranked fifth in 2014. In October 2020, at the national World Teachers' Day events in Abuja, it was named the best private secondary school in the country in the President's Teachers' and Schools Excellence Awards.
s019.c: The school is in Oba, Anambra State, about twenty minutes' drive from Asaba Airport.

s020.name: Charles Dale Memorial International School
s020.h: Charles Dale Memorial International School (CDMIS) is a secondary boarding school affiliated with Bereton Montessori School. Bereton's leadership decided, at its 25th anniversary in 2003, to open a secondary school so that pupils could continue their education there. Ground was broken in 2004, and the school opened on 30 September 2006. It is named in memory of Charles Dale for his contribution to education in Nigeria.
s020.a: The school has about 400 students and more than 45 teaching staff.
s020.c: The campus is at 12 Army Range Road, Igwuruta-Eneka, Port Harcourt, Rivers State. It has science and computer laboratories, a library, sports fields, and housing for students and staff.
s020.source_name: Wikipedia: Charles Dale Memorial International School

s022.name: Olashore International School
s022.h: Olashore International School is a private, co-educational boarding secondary school founded in 1994 by the late Oba Olashore. In January 2022 its board of trustees set up a five-member panel to investigate allegations about how the school handled a 2004 case of sexual assault involving its students; no findings had been published at the time the source was written.
s022.a: The school teaches both the Nigerian and British curricula, preparing students for examinations including the Cambridge IGCSE and the West African Senior School Certificate Examination.
s022.c: The school occupies a 60-hectare campus at Iloko-Ijesa, Osun State, about three hours' drive from Lagos.

s023.name: Mater Amabilis Secondary School
s023.h: Mater Amabilis Secondary School is a Catholic boarding high school run by the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Onitsha. It was founded on 15 January 1962 by Archbishop Charles Heerey. Its roots go back to 1905, when the traditional ruler of Umuoji, Igwe Okafor Ugwumba, invited Irish Catholic missionaries to the town. Bishop Joseph Shanahan sent the catechist Jacob Chukwuemeka Odiakosa, who built the Umuoji parish, and in the 1950s the parish priest, Father John Jordan, founded Our Lady's Teacher Training College there.
s023.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education with boarding.
s023.c: It is in Umuoji, Anambra State.

s024.name: Lumen Christi International High School
s024.h: Lumen Christi International High School is a Catholic boys' boarding school founded on 5 October 1986 by Patrick Ekpu, later Archbishop Emeritus of Benin. It is owned and run by the Catholic Diocese of Uromi.
s024.a: The school has a record in competitions and examinations. It won the Edo State Governorship Debate Award on 30 September 2015, and that year one of its graduates was named the overall best NECO candidate in Edo State. It has also won the LAPO science quiz competition.
s024.c: The school is at Ivue, Irrua, in Esan Central local government area, in the Esan heartland of Edo State.
s024.source_name: Wikipedia: Lumen Christi International High School

s025.name: Government College Ikorodu
s025.h: Government College Ikorodu is a co-educational public secondary school founded on 21 September 1974 and formally opened two days later by Brigadier Mobolaji Johnson, then governor of Lagos State. About 200 pioneer students were transferred from other Lagos secondary schools on the basis of that year's common entrance examination, and the school first used a temporary site on Obafemi Awolowo Way (then Agbowa Road). Its first principal was Olatunde Balogun.
s025.a: The college did well in its first years: in 1975 it was among five colleges whose students received scholarships from the commissioner for education, Chief Adeniran Ogunsanya.
s025.c: The college is in Ikorodu, Lagos State.

s027.name: Bridge House College
s027.h: Bridge House College (BHC) is an independent, co-educational sixth-form college established in 2004 to prepare school leavers aged 15 to 19 for university. It started with eight students who wanted to study in the United Kingdom. From 2007 it began preparing students for universities in other countries as well, including the US, Canada, the UAE, Ireland, Ghana and Nigeria.
s027.a: The college teaches Cambridge A levels, with a one-year AS route and a two-year A2 route. It is an accredited Cambridge examination centre and offers Cambridge teacher training. It has educated more than 2,500 students, including the children of expatriates living in Nigeria.
s027.c: The college began on Olagunsoye Oyinlola Street, 2nd Avenue, Ikoyi, Lagos, and moved to its permanent campus in 2014.

s028.name: Marygold International School
s028.h: Obinna and Janeth Weli started Marygold International School in 2002. It is privately run and takes boys and girls, as day students and boarders.
s028.a: The school covers every stage from crèche, toddler, pre-nursery and nursery through primary to secondary school, with departments for science, music, ICT, phonics and vocational studies.
s028.c: The main building is on Station Road in Elelenwo, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

s029.name: Louisville Girls High School, Ijebu-Itele
s029.h: Louisville Girls High School (LGHS) is a private Catholic girls' secondary school run by the Sisters of St Louis in Nigeria. It was established in 1998.
s029.a: The school has a strong examination record. WAEC named one of its students as having the second-best WASSCE results in the country in 2012, and another as third-best in 2018. Its students have also won the national Rising Star competitions for short stories (2018) and poetry (2019).
s029.c: The school is in Ijebu-Itele, Ogun State.
s029.source_name: Wikipedia: Louisville Girls High School, Ijebu-Itele

s030.name: Lisabi Grammar School
s030.h: Lisabi Grammar School (LGS) is a co-educational public secondary school and one of the oldest schools in Ogun State. It opened in September 1943 as Lisabi Commercial College at Ijoko, and became a grammar school in 1961. When it was founded, the old Egba Division (Abeokuta, Ifo, Egba Owode and Odeda) had only two secondary schools, Abeokuta Grammar School and Baptist Boys' High School, both founded by missions. Lisabi was established to meet the growing demand for secondary education.
s030.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education for boys and girls.
s030.c: The school is now at Idi-Aba, Abeokuta, Ogun State.

s031.name: St. Francis Catholic Secondary School
s031.h: St. Francis Catholic Secondary School (SFCSS) is a private Catholic secondary school founded in 1990 by Francis Cusimano and run by the North-West Africa Province of the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits).
s031.a: In 2014 its students finished second and third in the country in the NECO examination, and in 2015 it was ranked 20th among the top 100 schools in Nigeria.
s031.c: The school is in Idimu, Lagos.
s031.source_name: Wikipedia: St. Francis Catholic Secondary School

s032.name: Federal Science and Technical College, Awka
s032.h: Federal Science and Technical College, Awka (FSTC Awka) is a federal government school specialising in science and technology. It was established in May 2002, together with three other Federal Science and Technical Colleges in different parts of the country, as part of the Federal Unity College system.
s032.a: The college has technical, science, humanities and languages departments, together with vocational guidance and counselling. It is led by a principal with six vice-principals, covering administration, academics, student affairs and special duties.
s032.c: The college is in Awka, the capital of Anambra State.
s032.source_name: Wikipedia: Federal Science and Technical College, Awka

s033.name: Redeemer's International Secondary School
s033.h: Founded in 1997, Redeemer's International Secondary School belongs to the Christ the Redeemer's School Movement. It is privately owned and admits both boys and girls.
s033.a: In 2017 it was one of four Nigerian schools to receive the British Council's International School Award, and it was recognised for the best WASSCE results in 2015/16.
s033.c: The school is in Maryland, Lagos.

s035.name: Lagelu Grammar School
s035.h: Lagelu Grammar School is a public secondary school founded on 27 January 1958 by the former Ibadan District Council as a boys' school, and it is one of the oldest public grammar schools in Ibadan. It became co-educational in the mid-1970s. It is named after Lagelu, the legendary founder of Ibadan, and its motto is 'Semper Optimum' ('always the best'). Two of its former students have become governors of Oyo State.
s035.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education, mainly to day students.
s035.c: Its campus covers about 25 acres in the Oremeji, Agugu area of Ibadan, Oyo State.

s036.name: The Lagoon School
s036.h: The Lagoon School is a private girls' primary and secondary school. It was established in September 1995 in Surulere and later moved to Lekki.
s036.a: The school has about 700 students in its secondary section and 250 in its primary section, with about 100 staff. Its programme includes music and art alongside academic subjects.
s036.c: The school is in Lekki, Lagos State.

s037.name: Edo Technical College
s037.h: Edo Technical College, also known as Benin Technical College, is a public technical and vocational college. It was first established in Benin City in 1970 with support from the Canadian government, during the administration of Samuel Ogbemudia. Its Benin City campus, now Government Science and Technical College, was renovated under the World Bank-assisted SEEFOR programme.
s037.a: The college teaches technical and vocational skills to encourage self-employment and enterprise among young people in Edo State.
s037.c: It runs several campuses in different local government areas of Edo State, with its original campus in Benin City.

s038.name: Lebanese International School, Lagos
s038.h: The Lebanese International School is a private school commissioned in 1964 by the Lebanese embassy, which still oversees its board of trustees, of which the Lebanese ambassador is a member.
s038.a: The school teaches from kindergarten to grade 12, mainly following a British curriculum, with English as the language of instruction. Its facilities include an auditorium, computer laboratory, art room, indoor gymnasium, outdoor basketball court and biology, chemistry and physics laboratories.
s038.c: The school is in Yaba, Lagos.
s038.s: Students include Nigerians, Lebanese, Syrians, Indians, Pakistanis and Germans, and Lebanese students often switch between English and Arabic.

s039.name: Bishop Okoye Spiritan Secondary School
s039.h: Bishop Okoye Spiritan Secondary School (BOSSS) is a private, co-educational Catholic secondary school in the Catholic Diocese of Port Harcourt. It is owned and run by the Holy Ghost Fathers and Brothers (Spiritans) of the South East Province of Nigeria. It is named after Godfrey Okoye, the first bishop of Port Harcourt, who did much for education in south-eastern Nigeria.
s039.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education and takes boarders of all nationalities.
s039.c: The main campus covers more than 300 plots of land in the town of Afam, in Oyigbo local government area, Rivers State.
s039.source_name: Wikipedia: Bishop Okoye Spiritan Secondary School

s040.name: Mea Mater Elizabeth High School
s040.h: Mea Mater Elizabeth High School is a private secondary boarding school that opened in September 2004.
s040.a: The school is organised on a British-style pattern, with a junior school (years 7 to 9) and a senior school (years 10 to 12). It holds entrance examinations, including at a centre in Abuja.
s040.c: The school is in the village of Ojiagu, Agbani, Enugu State.
s040.s: Students belong to four houses, red, blue, green and yellow. They come from across Nigeria, including Lagos, Port Harcourt, Abuja and Warri, and from abroad, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, Ireland and Italy.
s040.source_name: Wikipedia: Mea Mater Elizabeth High School

s041.name: Isolog Schools
s041.h: Isolog Schools is a privately owned group of primary and secondary schools led by its chairman, Engineer Isaac Ogundipe, and its proprietor, Mrs Rachel Ogundipe.
s041.a: The group runs junior and senior schools, covering primary and secondary education.
s041.c: The main campus is in Akute, Ogun State, with a second campus at Ojodu in Lagos State.

s042.name: Norwegian International School, Port Harcourt
s042.h: The Norwegian International School (NIS) was set up in 1983 for the children of expatriate staff of Bulkcem Cement Company. It started with two teachers and about twelve pupils, and it has since grown to take children whose parents work for other companies.
s042.a: The school teaches children aged 2 to 16, from nursery to secondary school. Its curriculum draws on the English National Curriculum, the Cambridge International Primary Programme and the IGCSE.
s042.c: The school is in New GRA, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
s042.source_name: Wikipedia: Norwegian International School, Port Harcourt

s043.name: Grace Schools
s043.h: Grace Schools is a co-educational school founded in Gbagada, Lagos, in 1968 by Deaconess Grace Bisola Oshinowo. It added a high school in 1994.
s043.a: The school has four sections: nursery, primary, secondary and pre-university. Its facilities include a technical workshop, science laboratories, a library, art studios, a clinic, a multipurpose hall and a sports field, as well as a small zoo.
s043.c: The school is in Gbagada, Lagos.

s044.name: Bells Comprehensive Secondary School
s044.h: The Bells Comprehensive Secondary School for Boys and Girls is a private co-educational secondary school in Ota, run by the Bells Educational Foundation, which also founded Bells University of Technology.
s044.a: The school educates between about 500 and 1,000 students.
s044.c: The school is in Ota, Ogun State.

s045.name: Greenoak International School
s045.h: Greenoak International School (GIS) is a private primary and secondary school for children of all nationalities aged 5 to 16. Its primary school was founded in September 2004 and its secondary school in 2008.
s045.a: The school offers an international education that combines the International Primary Curriculum with American and British programmes. About a quarter of its students are expatriates and three-quarters are Nigerian.
s045.c: The school is in New GRA, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

s046.name: Lagos State Junior Model College Badore
s046.h: Lagos State Junior Model College, Badore is a state-owned junior secondary school. It was created on 6 January 2003, when the Lagos State Ministry of Education divided the state's secondary schools into separate junior and senior schools. It came from Lagos State Model College, Badore, founded on 19 February 1988, and its first principal was Mrs Sidikat Titilayo Smith.
s046.a: As a junior college it teaches the first three years of secondary school (JSS1 to JSS3).
s046.c: The school is in Badore village, in Eti-Osa local government area of Lagos State, and has hostels for its students.
s046.source_name: Wikipedia: Lagos State Junior Model College Badore

s047.name: KEY Academy
s047.h: KEY (Keep Educating Yourself) Academy is a private primary and secondary school founded in Lagos in 2019 by Damilola Okonkwo, a finance professional who previously worked at Credit Suisse and JP Morgan in London. She set it up as an alternative to the rote learning and memorisation common in Nigerian schools. In 2025 it was named a top-ten finalist for the World's Best School Prize for Innovation.
s047.a: The school is built around project-based learning, designed to develop skills such as problem-solving and collaboration. It takes children from 18 months to 18 years old.

s048.name: Archdeacon Crowther Memorial Girls' School
s048.h: Archdeacon Crowther Memorial Girls' School is an independent girls' secondary school. It is named after Archdeacon Dandeson Crowther, the Anglican churchman who led mission work in the Niger Delta.
s048.a: The school provides secondary education for girls.
s048.c: The school is in Elelenwo, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
s048.source_name: Wikipedia: Archdeacon Crowther Memorial Girls' School

s049.name: Aggrey Memorial Secondary School
s049.h: Aggrey Memorial Secondary School is a co-educational secondary school founded in 1931 by Alvan Azinna Ikoku, the educator, statesman and politician. Rather than name it after himself, Ikoku named it after James Emman Kwegyir Aggrey (1875–1927), the Ghanaian missionary and teacher.
s049.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education for boys and girls.
s049.c: The school is in Arochukwu, Abia State.

s050.name: The Regent School, Abuja
s050.h: The Regent School is a co-educational British school founded in 2000, originally for the children of British expatriates working in Abuja. It was the first British School Overseas (BSO) in Nigeria, and the first to receive an 'outstanding' inspection report from PENTA, an inspectorate approved by the UK Department for Education for British schools overseas.
s050.a: The school began by admitting primary pupils aged 2 to 11, and opened its senior school in 2007. It follows a British curriculum.
s050.c: The school is in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

s051.name: Baptist Girls' College, Abeokuta
s051.h: Baptist Girls' College (BGC) is a Baptist girls' secondary school founded about a century ago and affiliated with the Nigerian Baptist Convention. Like many mission schools, it was taken over by the government after the Nigerian Civil War, in the 1970s.
s051.a: The school provides secondary education for girls.
s051.c: The school is in the Idi-Aba area of Abeokuta, Ogun State.

s052.name: Italian International School Enrico Mattei
s052.h: The Italian International School 'Enrico Mattei', or Italian School Lagos, is an Italian international school. Italian education in Lagos goes back to the 1960s. The school's organisation bought its present site in February 1988, Italian companies built the classrooms and offices, which were finished in January 1991, and the sports facilities opened in May 1992.
s052.a: The school teaches from preschool through primary and lower secondary school to the liceo, the Italian upper secondary school.
s052.c: The campus covers 1.7 hectares in Lekki Phase I, Lagos. Its three-storey classroom block has a library, science laboratory, computer room and music room.
s052.source_name: Wikipedia: Italian International School Enrico Mattei

s053.name: Grait International College
s053.h: Grait International College is a privately owned secondary school established in 1995.
s053.a: The college takes both boys and girls, as day students and boarders.
s053.c: The school is in Sango-Ota, Ogun State, in south-western Nigeria.

s055.name: CITA International School
s055.h: CITA International School is a private Christian school founded on 15 May 1981. It began as a nursery and primary school, and added a high school section in 2001.
s055.a: CITA teaches children from six months to 16 years old, from nursery through primary to secondary school.
s055.c: The nursery and primary school is in the government residential area of Rumuogba, Port Harcourt. The secondary school is at Rumuochokota, in Etche local government area, Rivers State.

s056.name: Brookstone School Secondary
s056.h: Brookstone School Secondary is a private secondary school founded in 2006. Its name includes 'secondary' because Brookstone also runs a primary school at a separate site.
s056.a: The school teaches both British and Nigerian curricula, and its students sit international and local examinations, including Cambridge papers.
s056.c: The school is at Igwuruta, on the outskirts of Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
s056.s: Its colours are navy and sky blue. The four sports houses are named after precious stones: sapphire (blue), ruby (red), topaz (yellow) and emerald (green).

s057.name: St. Mary's Catholic Model High School
s057.h: St. Mary's Catholic Model High School opened its doors on 25 September 2006. Owned by the Catholic Bishop of Port Harcourt and managed by the Sisters of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, Mother of Christ, it takes boys and girls as both day students and boarders. Its motto is 'Faith, Knowledge and Love'.
s057.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education, with a chaplain attached to the school community.
s057.c: The school is in Port Harcourt, within the Catholic Diocese of Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
s057.source_name: Wikipedia: St. Mary's Catholic Model High School

s058.name: Uyo High School
s058.h: Uyo High School is a large government secondary school with about 5,000 students. In recent years it has faced cult-related unrest, and it was temporarily closed in June 2021 after a clash among students.
s058.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education as a public institution.
s058.c: The school is on Oron Road in Uyo, the capital of Akwa Ibom State.

s059.name: Government Science College, Dawakin Tofa
s059.h: Government Science College, Dawakin Tofa is a government science secondary school established in the 1970s to train students in the sciences and supply Kano State with well-qualified future doctors and engineers. In 2015 it was rated the best government-owned secondary school in Kano State.
s059.a: The school specialises in science education at secondary level.
s059.c: The school is in Dawakin Tofa local government area, Kano State.
s059.source_name: Wikipedia: Government Science College, Dawakin Tofa

s060.name: Titcombe College, Egbe
s060.h: Missionaries of the Sudan Interior Mission opened Titcombe College in March 1951. Its former students include Vice Admiral Samuel Afolayan, once Chief of Naval Staff, and the scholar Pius Adesanmi. Its alumni association has paid for several projects on the campus.
s060.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education.
s060.c: The college is in Egbe, Kogi State.

s061.name: Presentation National High School
s061.h: Presentation National High School is a Catholic girls' boarding school founded on 21 November 1989 by Archbishop Patrick Ebosele Ekpu of Benin City, with an initial intake of 60 girls. Its motto is 'Potestas ex Scientia' ('knowledge is power').
s061.a: The school placed 11th nationally in the 2006 West African Senior School Certificate Examination, and in 2016 the Nigerian Television Authority named it the best girls' school.
s061.c: The school is on Usunobun Street, Ugbekun Quarters, Benin City, Edo State.

s062.name: University of Ilorin Secondary School
s062.h: The University of Ilorin Secondary School is the staff secondary school of the University of Ilorin.
s062.a: In 2009 one of its students was the overall best candidate in the national NECO examinations.
s062.c: The school used to stand near the senior staff quarters on the university's permanent site, and moved to the university's mini campus in Ilorin, Kwara State, in 2012.
s062.source_name: Wikipedia: University of Ilorin Secondary School

s063.name: Cherryfield College
s063.h: Cherryfield College is a co-educational school following both Nigerian and British curricula, established in September 2004 for students from across Nigeria and beyond.
s063.a: The secondary school has about 300 students, all of them boarders.
s063.c: The college is in Jikwoyi, in the Federal Capital Territory.
s063.s: Students belong to four houses, each led by a prefect, and earn points, certificates and badges for good conduct.

s064.name: Jephthah Comprehensive Secondary School
s064.h: Jephthah Comprehensive Secondary School is a mixed secondary school founded by Mrs Ifeoma Chukwuogo on 6 October 1995.
s064.a: The school provides secondary education for boys and girls.
s064.c: The school is in Ozuoba, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

s065.name: Lutheran High School, Obot Idim
s065.h: Lutheran High School, Obot Idim is a Christian secondary school established in 1950, with Rev. John Louis Konz as its first principal. About 500 candidates sat its first entrance examination and only 28 passed. They began classes on the premises of Boechler Memorial Primary School, and by 1961 the school had grown to 348 students.
s065.a: The school keeps an average class size of about 20 students.
s065.c: The school is in Ibesikpo Asutan local government area, Akwa Ibom State.
s065.source_name: Wikipedia: Lutheran High School, Obot Idim

s066.name: Emmanuel Baptist College, Ilorin
s066.h: Emmanuel Baptist College is a private, mixed Baptist secondary school established by Emmanuel Baptist Church, Ilorin, on 9 October 2000. It is affiliated with the Nigerian Baptist Convention and run by a church committee, which appoints the principal.
s066.a: The college is an approved centre for the NECO SSCE and WASSCE examinations, and takes part in the Baptist mission schools' annual seminars and workshops.
s066.c: The school is at Tanke, Ilorin, Kwara State.

s067.name: Regina Pacis Model Secondary School
s067.h: Regina Pacis Model Secondary School is a Catholic girls' secondary school run by the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Onitsha. It was founded in 1962 by Archbishop Charles Heerey, and building work began in 1966.
s067.a: In 2018 a team of five of its students developed a fake-drug detection app, FD-Detector, which won a Junior Gold award, and in 2023 the school was invited to the Oxford Royale Academy summer programme in the United Kingdom.
s067.c: The school is in Onitsha, Anambra State.
s067.source_name: Wikipedia: Regina Pacis Model Secondary School

s068.name: Community Secondary School, Aka Offot
s068.h: Community Secondary School, Aka Offot is a government secondary school.
s068.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education.
s068.c: It is on Aka community road in Uyo local government area, Akwa Ibom State.
s068.source_name: Wikipedia: Community Secondary School, Aka Offot

s069.name: St. Anthony's Catholic High School, Ilesa
s069.h: St. Anthony's Catholic High School (SACHS) is a private Catholic secondary school founded by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Osogbo, after repeated requests from parents of pupils at the local Franciscan nursery and primary school. It was established in 1996 on a temporary site at the Ijofi-Ilesa Franciscan school, and began full operations in 1997.
s069.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education.
s069.c: The school is at Ijofi, Ilesa, Osun State. Its permanent site covers about 60 plots, roughly ten hectares.
s069.source_name: Wikipedia: St. Anthony's Catholic High School, Ilesa

s070.name: Christian Secondary Commercial School, Uyo
s070.h: Christian Secondary Commercial School is a government secondary school.
s070.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education.
s070.c: The school is in the city of Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.
s070.source_name: Wikipedia: Christian Secondary Commercial School, Uyo

s071.name: Dore Numa College
s071.h: Dore Numa College is a government-owned day secondary school established in October 1980 and named after Chief Dore Numa. Its motto is 'Hardwork Is Success'. In June 2013 the Delta State governor, Emmanuel Uduaghan, inspected the school among several new school buildings and criticised the vandalisation of government projects.
s071.a: The college provides secondary education to day students.
s071.c: The school is in Warri, Delta State.

s072.name: Niger Delta Science School
s072.h: Niger Delta Science School (NDSS), formerly OMPADEC Science Centre, is a specialist science secondary school.
s072.a: It is a senior secondary school only, teaching SS1 to SS3, with a focus on the sciences.
s072.c: The school is inside the main campus of the Rivers State College of Arts and Science at Rumuola, Port Harcourt.

s073.name: SunRise Sixth Form College
s073.h: SunRise Sixth Form College, also known as SunRise Academy, is a privately owned, co-educational sixth-form college for academically able students. It was founded to help Nigerian students go on to further education, and its results drew attention in 2006, when three of its seven candidates achieved straight A grades.
s073.a: The college offers full-time Cambridge AS and A-level courses to about 100 students, mostly aged 16 to 22, from Lagos and across Nigeria.
s073.c: The college is in Isolo, Lagos.

s075.name: Government Girls Science and Technical College, Potiskum
s075.h: Set up in 1979 to give girls in Yobe State access to science and technical education, Government Girls Science and Technical College, Potiskum is a state boarding school.
s075.a: The college has science, technical, computer, and humanities and arts departments.
s075.c: The school is in Potiskum, Yobe State.
s075.source_name: Wikipedia: Government Girls Science and Technical College, Potiskum

s076.name: Community Comprehensive Secondary School, Four Towns
s076.h: This government-run secondary school serves the Four Towns community in Uyo.
s076.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education.
s076.c: The school is in the Four Towns area of Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.
s076.source_name: Wikipedia: Community Comprehensive Secondary School, Four Towns

s077.name: Lagos State Junior Model College Kankon
s077.h: Lagos State Junior Model College, Kankon is a state-owned junior secondary school. It was created in 2003 from Lagos State Model College, Kankon, when the state reorganised its secondary schools into separate junior and senior schools.
s077.a: As a junior college it teaches JSS1 to JSS3. Like the other Lagos State model colleges, it is fully boarding.
s077.c: The school is in the Kankon area of Badagry, Lagos State.
s077.source_name: Wikipedia: Lagos State Junior Model College Kankon

s078.name: St. Brian's Model College, Uyo
s078.h: St. Brian's Model College is a Catholic secondary school that opened on 24 September 2000, with Lady Bernadette Martha Eyo as its first principal.
s078.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education.
s078.c: The school is in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.
s078.source_name: Wikipedia: St. Brian's Model College, Uyo

s079.name: Ikenne Community High School
s079.h: Ikenne Community High School is a secondary school founded in 1976 by the Ikenne community development association. It has educated more than ten thousand students.
s079.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education.
s079.c: The school is on the outskirts of Ikenne, in the Remo area of Ogun State, along the Sagamu-Benin expressway.
